chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) met Hudhayfa. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) extended his hand, but Hudhayfa withheld his hand. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Hudhayfa! I extended my hand to you, but you withheld your hand from me.' Hudhayfa said: 'O Messenger of Allah! In your hand is the desire (to greet me), but I was in a state of major ritual impurity (junub), so I did not like my hand to touch your hand while I was junub.' So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do you not know that when two Muslims meet and shake hands, their sins fall off just as the leaves of the tree fall off?'

key_terms.تَحَاتَّتْ ذُنُوبُهُمَا: Their sins fell off / were forgiven
key_terms.تَصَافَحَا: They shook hands / engaged in mutual greeting
key_terms.جُنُب: A state of major ritual impurity requiring full body wash (ghusl)
key_terms.حُذَيْفَة: Hudhayfa, a companion of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: Does one need to be in a state of ritual purity (taharah) to shake hands in Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) gently corrects Hudhayfa’s hesitation to shake hands while in a state of *junub* (major ritual impurity), establishing that the social bond of greeting holds independent spiritual merit. This incident is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between the ritual purity required for prayer and the permissibility of physical contact during other states of impurity, emphasizing that the act of *tasafuh* (handshaking) serves as a means for the shedding of sins, likened to leaves falling from a tree.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

having said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> met Huzayfa. So the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> extended his<sup>saww</sup> hand, but Juzayfa withheld his hand. So the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O Huzayfa! I<sup>saww</sup> extended my<sup>saww</sup> hand towards you, but you withheld your hand from me<sup>saww</sup>?’ So Huzayfa said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! In you hand is the desire (to greet me), but I was with sexual impurity, so I did not like my hand to touch yours<sup>saww</sup> while I was with sexual impurity’. So the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘But, do you not know that the Muslims, when two meet and shake hands, their sins fall off just like the falling off of the leaves of the tree?’
en.sarwar: 19. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ari from ibn al-Qaddah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Holy Prophet once met Hudhayfah and he extended his hand, but Hudhayfah held his hand back. The Holy Prophet asked, ‘How is it, O Hudhayfah, that I extended my hand to you and you held your hand back?’ Hudhayfah then said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, your hand is attractive but 1 had not taken the shower that was required of me due to carnal relations and I did not like to touch your hand with my hand that is not formally cleansed.’ The Holy Prophet then said, ‘Did you not know that when the Muslims meet and shake hands, their sins fall from them like leaves from trees?”’
